statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-120152 (PostgreSQL pg_show_all_settings() use-after-free discloses memory) in 17.12 on the PostgreSQL 17 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120152/ lists 17.12 as the fixed release for major version 17, and the 17.12 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/46c7529fa636d40c66cf6e99ffeea243181e6cdc on the REL_17_STABLE branch, which changes src/backend/utils/misc/guc_funcs.c so that show_all_settings(), behind the pg_show_all_settings() SQL function, materializes its whole result before any other expression in the query can run, instead of returning rows from a saved array of pointers to GUC entries that loading a module can free; it is tagged Security: CVE-2026-120152, and it is in the REL_17_12 release tag and not in REL_17_11. The DHI postgresql17 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD, currently https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/ce22298320177ae25085d86fbf3b4fc1150c16a2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; none of the patches it applies touch the source files this fix changes. We checked the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql17/postgres, in every published postgresql17 package for Alpine 3.23 on both x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): 17.12-r0 reports PostgreSQL 17.12 and carries the fix, while the earlier builds 17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0 and 17.11-r0 report 17.7, 17.8, 17.9, 17.10 and 17.11 and are affected. This fix adds no distinctive message string, so the per-build evidence is the version each server binary reports. 17.12-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix. Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD lists CVE-2026-120152 under its 17.12-r0 secfixes.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-120152, a use-after-free in pg_show_all_settings() that lets a database user read server memory, in 17.12. Major versions 16 to 18 are affected; within 17, releases before 17.12 are affected. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120152/, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.12-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6625-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-120152. The postgres server binary in this owner's 17.12-0 build and in its rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1 reports PostgreSQL 17.12 on amd64 and arm64, so both carry the fix, and 17.12-0 is the lowest published build that does. The 17.11-1 build and the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 report PostgreSQL 17.11, and the earlier rebuilds of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1 and 17.11-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, package PostgreSQL 17.10 and 17.11. All of these are affected and sort below 17.12-0.
